topic: Matrimonial Stream Triage — FJSS Pro Bono & Modest Means
user_query: Caller has a family or matrimonial matter (divorce, custody, maintenance, family violence). How do I triage this?
variations: Caller wants to file for divorce.
Caller is a foreigner married to a Singaporean.
Caller has a Syariah divorce matter.
Caller needs a lawyer for family court.
part_a_general_info: Reached from GEN3-T01 Route H. The Matrimonial Stream covers divorce (civil and Syariah), custody, care & control, maintenance, variation of court orders, and family violence applications (Personal Protection Orders). The two PBSG representation schemes here are FJSS (Pro Bono) and FJSS (Modest Means). FJSS (Pro Bono) eligibility: • Caller is a foreigner with at least one Singaporean child (the child must be below 21). • Caller faces matrimonial legal issue (including Syariah divorce, custody, maintenance, variation) covered by FJSS (if unsure, check with PBSG Staff). • Caller meets means test (https://www.probono.sg/get-legal-help/legal-representation/), financial documents will need to be submitted upon application. • Caller passes merits test (legal assessment on whether the case warrants representation, this will be done after application is submitted, intern/volunteer taking triaging call is NOT to reject based on their own assessment, no matter how unmeritorious the case appears to be). FJSS (Modest Means) eligibility: • Caller is a Singapore Citizen / PR who has marginally failed the Legal Aid Bureau's means test, OR a foreigner with at least one Singaporean child, who has marginally failed FJSS (Pro Bono)'s means test. • Caller faces matrimonial legal issue (including Syariah divorce, custody, maintenance, variation) covered by FJSS (if unsure, check with PBSG Staff). • Caller meets means test (https://www.probono.sg/get-legal-help/legal-representation/), financial documents will need to be submitted upon application. • Caller passes merits test (legal assessment on whether the case warrants representation, this will be done after application is submitted, intern/volunteer taking triaging call is NOT to reject based on their own assessment, no matter how unmeritorious the case appears to be).
triage_questions: Q1: Is there active or recent family violence (against the caller or a child), or is there court date/deadline within 14 days?
Q2: Is the caller a Singapore Citizen or PR?
Q3 (SGC/PR path): Has the caller applied to the Legal Aid Bureau (LAB) for civil legal aid?
Q4 (Foreigner path): Does the caller have at least one Singaporean child (under 21)?

Q5 (Means): Is the caller's Per Capita Household Income (PCHI) ≤ S$1,050, does the caller have savings of ≤ $10,000 if younger than 60 years old (or ≤ $40,000 if 60 years old or older), and does the caller stay in non-private housing (e.g. HDB, shelter, remand/prison)?

Q5A (if Q5 = No): Is the caller marginally above Pro Bono thresholds (PCHI ≤ S$1,400, savings ≤ $12,000 if younger than 60 years old or ≤ $48,000 if 60 years old or older, and in non-private housing), or clearly well above these thresholds?
branching_logic: Q1: Is there active or recent family violence (against the caller or a child), or is there court date/deadline within 14 days?
If Q1 = Yes → Route A (FJSS + Urgent concurrent — cross-reference GEN3-T06)
If Q1 = No → Proceed to Q2
If Q1 = Not Sure → Route A as precaution.
Q2: Is the caller a Singapore Citizen or PR?
If Q2 = Yes → Proceed to Q3 (LAB pathway first)
If Q2 = No (foreigner) → Proceed to Q4 (FJSS Pro Bono pathway)
If Q2 = Not Sure → Clarify nationality/residency status; if still unclear, Route F (Escalate to PBSG Staff).
Q3 (SGC/PR path): Has the caller applied to the Legal Aid Bureau (LAB) for civil legal aid?
If Q3 = No → Route B (Refer to LAB First)
If Q3 = Yes, passed LAB or LAB is processing → Route C (LAB is handling — PBSG not needed)
If Q3 = Yes, failed LAB means test → Proceed to Q5 (FJSS Modest Means path)
If Q3 = Not Sure → Route B for caller to check application status with LAB.
Q4 (Foreigner path): Does the caller have at least one Singaporean child (under 21)?
If Q4 = Yes → Proceed to Q5
If Q4 = No → Proceed to GEN3-T04 — Civil and Guidance Stream Triage
If Q4 = Not Sure → Clarify nationality/residency status; if still unclear, Route F (Escalate to PBSG Staff).

Q5 (Means): Is the caller's Per Capita Household Income (PCHI) ≤ S$1,050, does the caller have savings of ≤ $10,000 if younger than 60 years old (or ≤ $40,000 if 60 years old or older), and does the caller stay in non-private housing (e.g. HDB, shelter, remand/prison)?
(PCHI = total monthly household income ÷ number of persons in household, including the caller and all dependants.)
If Q5 = Yes (all within thresholds) → Route D (FJSS Pro Bono — Standard Intake)
If Q5 = No → Ask Q5A before routing.

Q5A (if Q5 = No): Is the caller marginally above Pro Bono thresholds (PCHI ≤ S$1,400, savings ≤ $12,000 if younger than 60 years old or ≤ $48,000 if 60 years old or older, and in non-private housing), or clearly well above these thresholds?
If Q5A = Marginally above thresholds → Route E (FJSS Modest Means)
If Q5A = Clearly well above thresholds → Proceed to GEN3-T04 — Civil and Guidance Stream Triage
If Q5A = Not Sure → Route F (Escalate to PBSG Staff).
If Q5 = Not Sure → Walk through the thresholds; if still unclear, take down figures and proceed to Route F (Escalate to PBSG Staff).

guardrail: • Under s 33 of the Legal Profession Act 1966, only qualified, practising lawyers may give legal advice. You must NEVER: (a) interpret a legal document for the caller; (b) apply the law to the caller's facts; (c) predict the outcome of a case; (d) tell the caller what they should do legally. • You MAY: (a) confirm scheme eligibility against objective criteria; (b) read out scheme descriptions verbatim; (c) explain PBSG hotline operations; (d) take down particulars and escalate to PBSG Staff. • If the caller insists on legal advice, respond: “I’m an intern/volunteer and I’m not able to give legal advice. What I can do is help you find the right legal help avenue or direct you to a qualified lawyer.” • If in doubt at any point — escalate to PBSG Staff. • Protect caller confidentiality. Do not discuss the caller outside the hotline context. Do not retain personal data on personal devices and/or beyond the PBSG volunteering period.
